literal: Except in those who drank, brewed liquor, like love, to those who see, causing joy, does not do.
translation: Brewed liquor does not, like love, cause delight to those who merely look at it; it only intoxicates those who actually drink it.
modern: காய்ச்சிய மதுவானது, காமத்தைப் போலத் தன்னை வெறும் கண்ணால் பார்த்தவர்களுக்கெல்லாம் மகிழ்ச்சியைத் தருவதில்லை; குடித்தவர்களுக்கு மட்டுமே அது மகிழ்ச்சியைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet compares the intoxicating power of brewed liquor (அடுநறா) with that of love (காமம்). Liquor is limited because it can only bring pleasure and intoxication to those who physically consume it. Love, however, is far more powerful as it brings instant joy and intoxication to those who merely look upon their beloved. Through this comparison, the poet highlights how the sight of the beloved alone is enough to induce a state of blissful intoxication.
